---
title: "Analyze the whole sample in DuckDB"
output: rmarkdown::html_vignette
---

```{r setup, message=FALSE}
library(easyNIS)
library(dplyr)
library(srvyr)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

The examples use invented data.

```{r means}
nis <- nis_open(nis_example(years = 2019:2020))
sample <- nis_survey(nis)
older <- filter(sample, AGE >= 65)

survey::svymean(~LOS, older)
survey::svyby(~LOS, ~YEAR, older, survey::svymean)
```

Use `nis_survey()` when your analysis spans a large share of the discharges.
`filter()` on the design defines a domain and keeps sampled hospitals in
the variance calculation. Means and totals, including grouped means and
totals, aggregate in DuckDB.

```{r model}
fit <- survey::svyglm(LOS ~ AGE + factor(YEAR), design = older)
summary(fit)$coefficients
```

Use additive `svyglm()` models with Gaussian identity, binomial or
quasibinomial logit, or Poisson or quasipoisson log families. Use
`nis_design()` for interactions, offsets, survey quantiles, chi-square
tests, srvyr summary verbs, and `tbl_svysummary()`.

## Estimate an average annual total

```{r annualize}
years <- nis |> distinct(YEAR) |> collect()
k <- nrow(years)
annual <- nis_survey(nis, weights = DISCWT / k)
survey::svytotal(~I(AGE >= 65), annual)
```

Use `k` equal to the number of years with valid design records. The example
has complete coverage. Keep `DISCWT` unscaled for separate annual totals.
[Years and coding eras](years-and-eras.html)
